neighbours.label: The spelling piece ' cas' / ' Cass' / ' Cas' opening a split word (Cass|iodorus, cas|ement, cas|uistry, Cas|pian), vs case, cast, casual, casino as single tokens
fire: On the old map, the Caspian is drawn far larger than it really is.
In the night sky she pointed out Cassiopeia above the barn.
The farmers grow cassava on the hillside plots.
From the upper casement a woman waved a white scarf.
The old film starred an aging Casanova who lost his charm.
Students read letters by Cassiodorus in the Latin seminar.
The priest hung his black cassock on a hook by the door.
He dismissed the argument as mere casuistry and left the room.
quiet: On the old map, the lake is drawn far larger than it really is.
In the night sky she pointed out the moon above the barn.
The farmers grow potatoes on the hillside plots.
From the upper window a woman waved a white scarf.
The old film starred an aging actor who lost his castle.
Students read letters by Cicero in the Latin seminar.
The priest hung his black coat on a hook by the door.
He dismissed the argument as a weak case and left the room.

predictions: ' cas'/' Cass'/' Cas'/' cass' as their own token reach 0.3-0.9; single-token words (case, cast, castle, casual, casino) in the same frames stay under 0.08.
short: ' cas' piece of a split word
